issues.legal_issue: A prima facie case of fabricating evidence in court proceedings, coupled with the expediency of action in the interests of justice, warrants a complaint for perjury.
material_facts: The application alleged that a balance sheet filed in the higher court proceedings had been altered by hand, changing the description of the share figures in a way that addressed a discrepancy relied on below.
The original balance sheet and other copies exhibited in the trial court record did not contain the handwritten alteration, while the copies filed in the higher court did.
The court found the altered wording materially significant because the original figures and the earnings-per-share calculation were based on the same share count despite an asserted share buy-back.

The company’s director had sworn to the veracity of the facts and documents filed in the higher court proceedings, although he had relied on the unaltered auditor’s report in his trial-court evidence.
The court found a prima facie case that evidence had been fabricated for the higher court proceedings and that action was expedient in the interests of justice.
issues.conclusion: The court allowed the application and directed an officer of the court to file complaints against the company and its director for perjury-related offences before a competent Magistrate.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 340 and 195(1)(b) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the court considers whether a prima facie case exists that an offence concerning evidence in a judicial proceeding has been committed and whether action is expedient in the interests of justice. The court relied on In Re: Suo Motu Proceedings against R. Karuppan, Advocate, (2001) 5 SCC 289, in directing an officer to file a complaint. It directed complaints under Sections 193 and 199 of the Indian Penal Code.

rule.if: perjury_proceeding and (court_record_versions_differ_materially and alteration_first_appeared_in_higher_court_filing) and alteration_could_mislead_court and action_expedient_in_justice

predicates.perjury_proceeding: The matter was an application seeking criminal action for alleged false evidence submitted in court proceedings.
predicates.court_record_versions_differ_materially: The court found that a document in the original lower-court record differed materially from the version filed in the higher court.
predicates.alteration_first_appeared_in_higher_cour: The court found that the alteration was absent from the versions exhibited below and appeared in the version filed in the higher court.
predicates.alteration_could_mislead_court: The alteration changed significant wording in a document in a way that could address an evidentiary discrepancy relevant to the proceedings.
predicates.action_expedient_in_justice: The court found that the circumstances made action appropriate in the interests of justice.

issues.definition: When an application concerns alleged false evidence in court proceedings, the court finds a material alteration first appearing in a higher-court filing that could mislead it, and action is expedient in the interests of justice, the court directs that a perjury complaint be filed.
